title: Human Reproductive System and Puberty
kicker: Cambridge Primary Checkpoint · Science 0097 · Stage 6 · Biology
summary: The parts of the male and female reproductive systems and what each one does, and the body changes of puberty — explained calmly and clearly, with growth-graph practice in Checkpoint style.

blocks.title: In the curriculum
items: Name the parts of the human reproductive system and say simply what each part does (6Bs.03)
Describe the physical (body) changes that happen to boys and girls during puberty (6Bp.01)

blocks.text: This page covers a topic that every person goes through: growing from a child into an adult. Scientists study it in the same calm, factual way that they study the heart or the lungs. Learn the correct scientific names — Checkpoint expects them, and using the proper words is the respectful way to talk about the human body.
1. The human life cycle

Every human goes through the same stages of life. The stage between being a child and being an adult is called **adolescence**. During adolescence the body goes through a set of changes called **puberty**. Puberty prepares the body so that, as an adult, a person is able to **reproduce** (have children). Reproduction is one of the life processes of all living things.

blocks.text: 2. Parts of the female reproductive system

The female reproductive system is inside the lower part of the body (the abdomen). Learn each part with its job. Checkpoint usually asks you to **name** a part from its job, or to **match** a part to its job.

rows: Makes and stores **egg cells**. After puberty, an egg cell is usually released about once a month.
**oviduct** (also called the egg tube or fallopian tube)
A tube that carries the egg cell from the ovary to the uterus.
A muscular organ where a baby grows and develops during pregnancy.
A ring of muscle at the lower end (the neck) of the uterus.
A muscular tube that leads from the cervix to the outside of the body.

blocks.title: Memory chain (female)
blocks.text: Follow the path of the egg cell: **ovary → oviduct → uterus**. The cervix and vagina are below the uterus. If you remember where the egg cell is made and where it travels, you can place every part in order.
3. Parts of the male reproductive system

rows: A bag of skin that holds the testes outside the body, where it is slightly cooler. Sperm cells develop best a little below body temperature.
A tube that carries sperm cells from the testes towards the penis.
Add a fluid to the sperm cells. The sperm cells and fluid together are called semen.
A tube inside the penis. It carries urine out of the body, and in adults it can also carry semen — but never both at the same time.
The organ that the urethra passes through.

blocks.title: Memory chain (male)
blocks.text: Follow the path of the sperm cell: **testis → sperm duct → urethra** (inside the penis). Glands add fluid on the way.

rows: Organ that makes the sex cell
Tube that carries the sex cell

blocks.text: 4. Puberty: what changes and why

Puberty is started by **hormones**. Hormones are chemicals made in the body that travel in the blood and tell organs to change. Puberty usually begins between about 8 and 13 years old in girls and between about 9 and 14 in boys, and it lasts a few years. Everyone is different: starting earlier or later than a friend is completely normal.
Some changes happen to **both** boys and girls, and some happen to only one. Checkpoint often gives a list of changes and asks you to sort them, so learn the table below.

headers: Changes in both boys and girls
rows: voice becomes deeper (the voice 'breaks') because the voice box grows
hair grows under the arms and in the pubic area
hair grows on the face (beard and moustache)
skin becomes more oily; spots (acne) may appear
shoulders and chest become broader; muscles grow bigger
more sweat is produced, so body odour can start
the ovaries begin to release egg cells
the testes begin to make sperm cells

blocks.text: Puberty can also bring **emotional** changes, such as mood changes or caring more about how you look. These are real and normal, but the objective asks about **physical** changes — so if a question says 'physical change', do not write a feeling.

blocks.title: Good hygiene during puberty
blocks.text: Because sweat and oil increase, it becomes more important to wash every day, wear clean clothes, use deodorant if you wish, and wash your face to help with spots. This links to the Diseases and Hygiene page.
5. Reading a growth graph

blocks.caption: Karim's height measured on each birthday from age 8 to 16.

items: Read the axes first: x-axis = age in years, y-axis = height in cm. Each small square on the height axis is **5 cm**.
To find the growth in one year, subtract: height at the later age − height at the earlier age.
The **steepest** part of the line shows the fastest growth — this is the growth spurt of puberty.
Near the end the line becomes flatter: growth slows down as the body reaches adult height.

blocks.text: Worked examples
**Worked example 1** — Name the organ in a female that makes egg cells. [1 mark]

items: Egg cells are the female sex cells.
They are made and stored in the ovaries.

blocks.text: **Answer:** ovary. **Common mistake:** writing 'uterus' or 'womb'. The uterus is where a baby develops — it does not make eggs.

**Worked example 2** — Draw a line to match each part to its job. Parts: testis, sperm duct, scrotum. Jobs: (i) carries sperm cells away from the testes; (ii) makes sperm cells; (iii) holds the testes outside the body. [2 marks]

items: Testis → makes sperm cells (ii).
Sperm duct → carries sperm cells away (i). The word 'duct' means tube.
Scrotum → holds the testes outside the body (iii).

blocks.text: **Answer:** testis–(ii), sperm duct–(i), scrotum–(iii). Mark schemes often give 2 marks for all three correct and 1 mark for one correct.
**Worked example 3** — Here are four changes: voice gets deeper; growth spurt; breasts develop; hair grows under the arms. Which **two** changes happen to both boys and girls? [1 mark]

items: Voice getting deeper — boys only.
Breasts develop — girls only.
Growth spurt and underarm hair — both.

blocks.text: **Answer:** growth spurt **and** hair grows under the arms (both needed for the mark).
**Worked example 4** — Use the table of Karim's heights. (a) How much did Karim grow between age 12 and age 13? (b) Between which two birthdays did he grow the most? [2 marks]

items: (b) Work out every yearly increase: 5, 5, 5, 7, 8, 7, 4, 2 cm. The largest is 8 cm.
So the biggest growth was between ages **12 and 13**.

blocks.text: **Answer:** (a) 8 cm (b) between 12 and 13. **Common mistake:** choosing the highest point on the graph (age 16). The tallest height is not the fastest growth — look for the biggest increase.
**Worked example 5** — Explain why the growth line on Karim's graph becomes flatter after age 15. [1 mark]
**Answer:** puberty is nearly finished, so his growth is slowing down / he is reaching his adult height. (Do not write 'he stopped eating' — use the science of puberty.)

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Mixing up **ovary** (makes eggs) and **uterus** (where a baby develops).
Writing 'testicle' and 'testes' wrongly: one **testis**, two **testes** (testicles is also accepted).
Mixing up the **urethra** (tube through the penis) with the **sperm duct** (tube from the testis).
Giving a feeling (such as 'moody') when the question asks for a **physical** change.
Thinking that all changes happen to everyone: periods and breasts are girls only; a deeper voice and facial hair are boys only.
On a growth graph, choosing the tallest point instead of the biggest increase.

blocks.title: How Checkpoint asks this
items: **Name the part** that does a job — one word, spelt clearly (phonetic spelling is usually credited, but learn the correct spelling).
**Match** parts to their jobs with lines — check that every line goes to only one box.
**Sort** changes into a table: boys only / girls only / both. Tick every box that applies.
**Read a growth graph or table**: work out a change in height and show the subtraction.
**Explain** a change in one short sentence, using a key word such as 'hormones' or 'puberty'.

blocks.title: القاعدة اللي لازم تفتكرها
blocks.text: البلوغ (puberty) بيبدأ بسبب الهرمونات (hormones). فيه تغييرات للولاد والبنات الاتنين (طول سريع growth spurt، شعر تحت الإبط، عرق وحبوب)، وتغييرات للبنات بس (الدورة الشهرية periods، الصدر، الأرداف)، وتغييرات للولاد بس (الصوت يتخن، شعر الدقن، الكتاف تعرض). لو السؤال قال physical change متكتبش إحساس زي moody.
Practice

blocks.title: Human Reproductive System and Puberty — Practice
blocks.intro: 13 Checkpoint-style questions. Answer, check, then read each full solution. Open questions are self-marked against the mark scheme.

questions.e: Sperm cells are made in the testes (one testis). The sperm duct and urethra are tubes that carry them; the scrotum only holds the testes.

questions.q: Name the part of the female reproductive system where a baby grows and develops during pregnancy.
questions.e: The uterus (womb) is the muscular organ where a baby develops. The ovary makes eggs; the oviduct carries eggs.

questions.q: Name the tube that carries an egg cell from the ovary to the uterus.
questions.e: The oviduct (egg tube, fallopian tube) carries the egg cell from the ovary to the uterus.

questions.q: What starts the changes of puberty?
questions.e: Hormones — chemical messengers carried in the blood — start the changes of puberty.

questions.q: Which change happens during puberty in girls **only**?
questions.e: Periods begin in girls only. A growth spurt, underarm hair and oilier skin happen in both boys and girls.

questions.q: Which change happens during puberty in boys **only**?
questions.e: The voice box grows in boys, so the voice becomes deeper. The other three changes happen in both boys and girls.

questions.p:
Question 7
The male reproductive system has a tube inside the penis that carries urine out of the body.
questions.e: The urethra carries urine (and, in adults, semen — never both at the same time). Do not confuse it with the sperm duct.

questions.q: Explain why the testes are held in the scrotum, outside the body.
questions.ms: 1 mark: it is cooler outside the body / sperm cells develop best a little below body temperature. Accept 'to keep the testes cool'. Do not accept 'for protection' alone.
questions.e: The scrotum keeps the testes slightly cooler than the inside of the body, and sperm cells develop best at this slightly lower temperature.

questions.q: (b) Between which two birthdays did Salma grow the most? Write the two ages, for example 9 and 10.
questions.e: Yearly increases: 9→10: 5 cm; 10→11: 7 cm; 11→12: 8 cm; 12→13: 4 cm. The largest is 8 cm, between ages 11 and 12.

questions.p:
Question 9
Salma's height was measured on each birthday.
Age 9: 131 cm
Age 10: 136 cm
Age 11: 143 cm
Age 12: 151 cm
Age 13: 155 cm
questions.q: (c) Salma says: "I grew most between 11 and 12 because of puberty." Use science to explain what she means.
questions.ms: 1 mark: puberty includes a growth spurt / she grew quickly because puberty (hormones) started. Do not accept 'she ate more'.
questions.e: One of the physical changes of puberty is a growth spurt: hormones make the body grow taller quickly for a few years.

questions.q: Give **two** physical changes that happen to both boys and girls during puberty.
questions.ms: 1 mark each, any two: growth spurt / grow taller quickly; hair grows under the arms; pubic hair grows; skin becomes more oily / spots (acne); more sweat / body odour. Do not accept emotional changes (e.g. mood changes). Do not accept changes for one sex only (e.g. deeper voice, periods).
questions.e: For example: a growth spurt, and hair growing under the arms. Others: pubic hair, oilier skin and spots, more sweat.

questions.q: Which list shows the path of an egg cell in the correct order?
questions.e: The egg cell is made in the ovary, travels along the oviduct and reaches the uterus.

blocks.title: Remember
items: Female: **ovary** (makes eggs) → **oviduct** (carries egg) → **uterus** (baby develops) → cervix → vagina.
Male: **testis** (makes sperm) in the **scrotum** → **sperm duct** → **urethra** in the penis; glands add fluid.
**Puberty** is the set of body changes in adolescence, started by **hormones**.
Both: growth spurt, body hair, oilier skin, more sweat. Girls only: breasts, wider hips, periods. Boys only: deeper voice, facial hair, broader shoulders.
On a growth graph, the **steepest** part = fastest growth (the growth spurt).
